JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 14-05-2019 at about 7.30 p.m., the petitioner was returning to his village from Oballapura, via service road, on his motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EN-3238, slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations.

At that time, near J.G.
Halli Junction, Hiriyur Taluk, Chitradurga, when he was taking turn towards NH-4 road, leading towards Bengaluru side, suddenly the driver of a Swift car bearing No.
KA-05-MN-1944, came from Bengaluru side in a rash and negligent manner, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Hemavathi Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, S.S. Puram, Tumkur, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.

sentences.text: Earlier to the accident, he was working as milk vendor and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Hiriyur Rural Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences Sureshanaik.

2 punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.

The respondent No.1 is the owner,
respondent No.2 is the policy holder and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.3 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondents No.1 and 2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.3 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of car bearing No. KA-05-MN- 1944.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has further contended that, the driver of the offending car was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
It has denied the very occurrence of the accident and involvement of the car.

The car in question has neither involved in the accident,
nor it has caused accidental injuries to the petitioner
. The petitioner has sustained injuries due to self fall from motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EN-3238.
It has contended that, as on the date of accident, the car was being driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of the car.

The accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner, who without having proper look out at the vehicular movements of the road, without noticing on coming vehicles, rode the motorcycle recklessly and carelessly and caused the accident.
It has further contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties to the petition.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries due to the Road Traffic Accident, alleged to have occurred on 14-05-2019 at about 7:30 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Swift Car, bearing registration No.
KA-05-MN-1944?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

3 6.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to 12.
Further, he has got examined one more witness namely Dr. Chidanand K.J.C. as P.W.2 and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.3 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 14-05-2019 at about 7.30 p.m., the petitioner was returning to his village from Oballapura, via service road, on his motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EN-3238, slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations.

At that time, near J.G. Halli Junction, Hiriyur Taluk, Chitradurga, when he was taking turn towards NH-4 road, leading towards Bengaluru side, suddenly the driver of a Swift car bearing No.
KA-05-MN-1944, came from Bengaluru side in a rash and negligent manner, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as milk vendor and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 12 documents as Ex.
P.1 to 12

. Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.3 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.4 is true copy charge- sheet, Ex.P.5 is discharge summary, Ex.P.6 are prescriptions (total 18), Ex.P.7 are medical bills (total 23), Ex.P.8 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.9 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.10 is notarised copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.11 is valuation slip and Ex.P.12 is X-ray.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 4, 8 and 9, prima-facia it reveals that, on 14-05-2019 at about 7.30 p.m., near J.G. Halli Junction, Hiriyur Taluk,
Chitradurga, when the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EN-3238, slowly and cautiously and taking turn towards NH-4 road, leading towards Bengaluru side, suddenly the driver of a offending car bearing No. KA-05-MN-1944, came from Bengaluru side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

The investigation officer in his final Sureshanaik.R.L. Alias Sureshanayaka ... vs Viresh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127269993/
4 report, marked as Ex.P.4, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-MN- 1944 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

12. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending car bearing No. KA-05-MN-1944 in the alleged accident and issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of car bearing No. KA-05-MN-1944 and its validity as on the date of accident, is not in dispute.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner and policy holder of offending vehicle bearing No. KA-05-MN-1944 i.e. respondent No.1 & 2, as they did not choose to appear and contest the case of petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.3 insurance company though has specifically denied the said facts in its written statement and taken specific defence that, the car bearing No. KA-05-MN-1944 is not at all involved in the alleged accident and the same has occurred due to self negligence of the petitioner, it has not produced any evidence to establish the said contentions or rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Even, the respondent No.3 has not stepped into witness box to depose the contentions taken in its written statement on oath.

The petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestions made in his cross-examination by the learned counsel for respondent No.3 that, the said accident has occurred due to his self rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle and taking sudden u-turn at the place of accident, there is no fault on the part of driver of offending car bearing No. KA- 05-MN-1944 and in order to claim compensation he has lodged false complaint against the said driver.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.3 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

There is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the petitioner has sustained injuries due to his own rash and negligent riding and self fall from the motorcycle and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending car bearing Reg. No.
KA-05-MN-1944.
13.
It seems very strange to note that, the respondent No.3 has taken contrary stand in the case.

At one point, in its written statement, the respondent No.3 has taken specific defence that, the offending car bearing No. KA-05- MN-1944 is not at all involved in the alleged accident and the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner and self fall from the motorcycle.

Whereas, at the other point, in the same written statement, the respondent No.3 has contended that, at the time of accident the driver of offending car was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle and hence, it is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 with respect to present claim petition.

Further, he has contended that, at the time of accident, the driver of offending car was driving in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness and negligence on the part of said driver.

14. The Ex.P.9 spot mahazer also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on Bengaluru-Chitraduraga NH-4 road, near J.G. Halli Junction, Hiriyur Taluk, Chitradurga, due to dashing of offending car proceeding from Bengaluru side to the motorcycle of petitioner, when he was taking u-turn from service road to join national highway.
The investigation officer in his Ex.P.4 final report has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent Sureshanaik.

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127269993/
5 driving of the offending car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-MN-1944.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.2, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.
KA-05-MN-1944.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.3 and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to self rash and negligent riding of the petitioner or there was any contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner in the cause of accident.
Further, the Ex.P.4 final report/charge-sheet filed by the investigation officer has not been challenged either by the owner or the driver of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident 15.

Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.3 wound certificate, Ex.P.5 discharge summary,
Ex.P.11 valuation slip and Ex.P.12 X-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered Type II fracture both bones right leg.
The same is deposed by P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.3, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that,
the respondent No.3 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-MN-1944.
16.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text: 17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others

18. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 14-05-2019 at about 7:30 p.m., near J.G. Halli Junction, Hiriyur Taluk, Chitradurga, due to rash and negligent driving of the Sureshanaik.

sentences.text: Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Swift car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-MN-1944 and he has sustained Type II fracture both bones right leg and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport,
actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.10.
As per Ex.P.10, the year of birth of the petitioner is 1992.
The accident has taken place on 14-05- 2019 at about 7:30 p.m.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 27 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered Type II fracture both bones right leg.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has 42%
physical disability of right lower limb and 14% physical disability for the whole body.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.3 wound certificate,
Ex.P.5 discharge summary, Ex.P.11 valuation slip and Ex.P.12 X-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered Type II fracture both bones right leg.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.3 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.
Further he has denied that, there are no restrictions of movements to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 14-05-2019 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 25-01-2024, which is after lapse of four years and seven months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the fracture is united.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 9% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 9% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

7 a)
The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as milk vendor and was earning income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do milk vending work.
The respondent No.3 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was doing milk vending work.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2019.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.14,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,68,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 27 years is 17.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,68,000 X 9/100 X 17 = Rs.2,57,040/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.1,50,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 23 medical bills, as per Ex.P.7.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.75,943/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.75,943/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
suffered Type II fracture both bones right leg.
As per Ex.P.5 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 09 days from 14-05-2019 to 22-05-2019, in Hemavathi Orthopaedic & Trauma Centre, Bengaluru.
Further, as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner,
this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:

As per Ex.P.5 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 09 days from 14-05-2019 to 22-05-2019, in Hemavathi Orthopaedic & Trauma Centre,
Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 9 = Rs.9,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:

As per Ex.P.5 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 09 days from 14-05-2019 to 22-05-2019, in Hemavathi Orthopaedic & Trauma Centre,
Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 9 = Rs.7,200/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The accident has taken place near J.G. Halli Junction, Hiriyur Taluk,
Chitradurga and the petitioner has taken treatment at Hemavathi Orthopaedic & Trauma Centre,
Sureshanaik.

sentences.text: Taking into consideration the distance in between both the places, compensation of Rs.4,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 9 days as inpatient at Hemavathi Orthopaedic & Trauma Centre, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.14,000 x 2 = Rs.28,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:
It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 27 years and unfortunately he has suffered Type II fracture both bones right leg.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 9% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants for which approximate cost of Rs.25,000/- is required.
The P.W.2 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery or for further treatment.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

20. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 2,57,040-00 2.
Medical expenses 75,943-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00
4. Attendant charges 9,000-00 5.
Food and nourishment 7,200-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 4,000-00 7. Loss of income during 28,000-00 treatment period 8.
Loss of amenities 20,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses 20,000-00 Total Rs. 4,61,183-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,61,183/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

9 21.
Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent No.2 is the policy holder and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-05-MN-1944 the said accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.3 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondents No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.3 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,61,183/- from the respondent No.3, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.4,61,183/- (Rupees four lakh sixty one thousand one hundred and eighty three only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.3 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of petitioner as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
The respondent No.1 is the owner,
respondent No.2 is the policy holder and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries due to the Road Traffic Accident, alleged to have occurred on 14-05-2019 at about 7:30 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Swift Car, bearing registration No.
KA-05-MN-1944?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
18. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 14-05-2019 at about 7:30 p.m., near J.G. Halli Junction, Hiriyur Taluk, Chitradurga, due to rash and negligent driving of the Sureshanaik.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Whereas, the respondent No.3 insurance company though has specifically denied the said facts in its written statement and taken specific defence that, the car bearing No. KA-05-MN-1944 is not at all involved in the alleged accident and the same has occurred due to self negligence of the petitioner, it has not produced any evidence to establish the said contentions or rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.
KA-05-MN-1944.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.3 and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to self rash and negligent riding of the petitioner or there was any contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner in the cause of accident.
Further, the Ex.P.4 final report/charge-sheet filed by the investigation officer has not been challenged either by the owner or the driver of offending vehicle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident 15.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that,
the respondent No.3 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-MN-1944.
16.
Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.
If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 9% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 9% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was doing milk vending work.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2019.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.14,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,68,000/-.
b)
The respondent No.3 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.
20. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 2,57,040-00 2.
Medical expenses 75,943-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00
4. Attendant charges 9,000-00 5.
Conveyance expenses 4,000-00 7. Loss of income during 28,000-00 treatment period 8.
Loss of amenities 20,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses 20,000-00 Total Rs. 4,61,183-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,61,183/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
Therefore, the respondents No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.3 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,61,183/- from the respondent No.3, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.4,61,183/- (Rupees four lakh sixty one thousand one hundred and eighty three only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.3 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of petitioner as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
